analysis: The method queueInputBuffer first calls checkState which may throw IllegalStateException (a runtime exception) if the stream has ended. Then it computes offset, size, and flags. The call to mediaCodec.queueInputBuffer may throw MediaCodec.CodecException (a runtime exception). After the call, it updates inputBufferIndex and clears inputBuffer.data. Currently, no exception handling is present. If mediaCodec.queueInputBuffer throws an exception after inputStreamEnded has been set to true, the state becomes inconsistent. It is therefore advisable to catch the runtime exception from the codec call, revert the state change (inputStreamEnded) if necessary, and rethrow the exception to maintain consistency. No other parts need catching as they indicate programming errors.
